Past continuous ('was doing' / verb stem + rahaa thaa)

completed_lessons.title: Conversational Connectors, Discourse Markers & Improv Fillers

Improv reactions and banter (arre yaar, sach mein?, sahi baat hai, bilkul)
Chronological sequencers (pehle, phir, uske baad, aakhiri mein)

completed_lessons.title: Expressing Opinions, Impressions & Mental States
concepts: Opinion framing formulas (Mujhe lagtaa hai ki, Mere khayaal se, Meraa maannaa hai ki)
Dative experiencer alignment with Tamil (Enakku thonrudhu)
Nuances of certainty and probability (Zaroor, Pakkaa, Ho saktaa hai, Shaayad, Pakkaa nahin)
Polite agreement & soft disagreement (Sahi baat hai, Yeh point sahi hai, Mujhe aisaa nahin lagtaa)

mastered_patterns: SOV sentence structure alignment from Tamil
Present habitual with male conjugation (-taa hoon)
Core postpositions (me, par, se, ke saath, ke liye)
Oblique shifts on masculine nouns (kamre me, Shivani se milne ke liye)
Clause linking with Ki vs Kaa/Ke/Kee
Obligation structures with padtaa hai and jaanaa hai
Communication verbs distinction (Bolna vs Baat karna)
Shopping expressions, price inquiries, and -vaalaa demonstratives
Ergative case marker (Ne) and dynamic object agreement
Conversational connectors, fillers, and improv reactions (Matlab, Vaise, Yaani, Sahi baat hai)
Opinion framing with dative experiencer (Mujhe lagtaa hai ki...) and thoughtful viewpoints (Mere khayaal se...)
Nuances of certainty, probability, and polite disagreement in natural Hinglish
active_struggles: Oblique shifts on compound phrases or demonstratives before rapid speech
Quick mental recall of Hindi cardinal numbers between 15 and 30 in rapid spoken conversation
Fluid spontaneous use of 'Ho saktaa hai ki...' vs 'Shaayad' in rapid discourse
